questions.explanation: Hospitality covers accommodation, food and beverage, and related services.

options: a mixture of fat and flour
getting everything ready before cooking or service
questions.explanation: Mise en place = "everything in its place": preparation before work.

questions.stem: A fire caused by burning cooking oil in a kitchen should be put out with
questions.explanation: Water on burning oil spreads the fire violently; smothering removes oxygen.

questions.stem: Which extinguisher is suitable for a fire involving electrical equipment?
questions.explanation: CO2 does not conduct electricity and leaves no residue.

questions.stem: To prevent slips and falls in a busy kitchen, staff should
options: wipe up spills immediately and wear non-slip shoes
questions.explanation: Clean floors and suitable footwear prevent slips.

questions.stem: Cooked food should be kept out of the "danger zone", which is between about
questions.explanation: Bacteria multiply rapidly between about 5 °C and 60 °C (some food codes use 63 °C as the upper limit).

questions.stem: A food handler with a cut on the finger should
options: cover it with a waterproof (blue) plaster before handling food
cover it with an ordinary cloth
questions.explanation: Waterproof coloured plasters prevent contamination and are easy to spot if lost.

questions.stem: Keeping raw meat and cooked foods apart, and using separate boards and knives for each, mainly prevents
questions.explanation: Bacteria from raw foods can spread to ready-to-eat foods.

questions.explanation: Pulses are dried edible seeds of legumes.

questions.explanation: Long cooking of fish bones extracts bitter flavours.

questions.topic: Principles of cooking methods and practical demonstrations
questions.stem: Grilling is most suitable for
options: tender, good-quality cuts of meat and fish
questions.explanation: Grilling is fast dry heat; tough cuts need long moist cooking.

questions.topic: Principles of cooking methods and practical demonstrations
questions.stem: Placing meat in boiling liquid at the start of cooking, rather than in cold liquid, helps to
options: seal the surface and retain the juices and flavour in the meat
extract maximum flavour into the liquid for stock
questions.explanation: Starting in boiling liquid coagulates surface proteins; cold-start is used for stocks.

questions.explanation: At a buffet guests serve themselves.

questions.topic: Types of food service and table laying/setting
questions.stem: Service in which food is finished or flambeed on a side table or trolley in front of the guest is
questions.explanation: Gueridon service uses a trolley for carving, flambeing or finishing dishes.

questions.topic: Types of food service and table laying/setting
questions.stem: A table d'hote cover differs from an a la carte cover in that it
options: is laid only after the guest has finished
has all the cutlery needed for the set menu laid before the meal
questions.explanation: A table d'hote cover is laid for the whole set menu; a la carte cutlery is laid according to dishes ordered.

questions.explanation: A salamander gives intense top heat for browning.

options: keeping food hot or cooking gently in a container of hot water
questions.explanation: The water bath provides gentle, even heat.

questions.topic: Care and maintenance of kitchen equipment
questions.stem: Before cleaning an electric meat slicer, the operator must first
options: remove the safety guard while running
switch it off and unplug it
questions.explanation: Isolating the power prevents serious injury.

questions.topic: Care and maintenance of kitchen equipment
questions.stem: A new cast-iron frying pan is "seasoned" by
options: heating it with a thin coating of oil
questions.explanation: Seasoning forms a protective non-stick layer and prevents rusting.

questions.stem: Which of the following should be considered when planning a menu for a restaurant?
options: The colour of the restaurant roof
The type of customers and the skills of the kitchen staff
The number of car parks in town
questions.explanation: Customers, cost, staff skill, equipment and season influence menus.

questions.stem: A menu on which each dish is priced separately and cooked to order is
questions.explanation: A la carte dishes are individually priced; table d'hote is a fixed-price set menu.

questions.stem: The "plat du jour" on a menu means the
questions.explanation: Plat du jour = a special dish of the day.

questions.stem: A lacto-vegetarian eats
options: plant foods and milk products but no meat, fish or eggs
plant foods only and no milk
questions.explanation: Lacto-vegetarians include dairy; lacto-ovo vegetarians also eat eggs; vegans eat no animal products.

questions.stem: The traditional sauce served with roast lamb is
questions.explanation: Mint sauce goes with lamb; apple sauce with pork; tartare sauce with fried fish.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a table accompaniment?
questions.explanation: Table accompaniments are placed on the table for guests to add, e.g. salt, pepper, sauces.

questions.stem:
(a) State four causes of accidents in a commercial kitchen. [4 marks]
(b) Name the most suitable fire-fighting equipment for (i) a fat fire in a frying pan; (ii) a fire in an electrical appliance. [2 marks]
(c) State two ways of preventing burns and scalds in the kitchen. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
4 marks: Any four (1 each): wet or greasy floors; carelessness/rushing; faulty electrical equipment; poor lighting; blunt or wrongly used knives; obstructions in walkways; lack of training; overcrowding
1 mark: Fat fire: fire blanket (accept wet chemical extinguisher)
1 mark: Electrical fire: CO2 or dry powder extinguisher (after switching off power)
2 marks: Any two (1 each): use dry oven cloths; turn pan handles inward; do not overfill pans; warn others when carrying hot items; lower food gently into hot oil
questions.explanation: Accidents result from wet floors, carelessness, faulty equipment and poor lighting. Use a fire blanket for fat fires and CO2/dry powder for electrical fires. Prevent burns with dry cloths, inward handles and care with hot oil.

questions.stem:
(a) State four personal hygiene practices required of a food handler. [4 marks]
(b) State four food safety practices for the storage and handling of cooked food. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
4 marks: Any four (1 each): wash hands frequently; wear clean uniform and cover hair; keep nails short with no polish; cover cuts with waterproof plaster; do not work when ill; no smoking or spitting; avoid wearing jewellery
4 marks: Any four (1 each): keep hot food above about 60-63 °C and cold food below 5 °C; cool quickly and refrigerate; cover food; store raw and cooked food separately; reheat thoroughly once only; use clean utensils; label and date stored food
questions.explanation: Food handlers must wash hands, wear clean uniforms, cover hair and cuts and stay off work when ill. Keep food out of the 5-60 °C danger zone, cover it, separate raw and cooked items and reheat once thoroughly.

questions.topic: Principles of cooking methods and practical demonstrations
questions.stem:
(a) What is roasting? [2 marks]
(b) State three principles to observe when roasting meat. [3 marks]
(c) Name the traditional accompaniments for (i) roast beef; (ii) roast pork; (iii) roast chicken. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Cooking food in dry heat with fat in an oven or on a spit, basting regularly
3 marks: Any three (1 each): use tender cuts; start in a hot oven to seal then reduce heat; baste regularly; place on a trivet/rack; rest meat before carving; cook to the correct internal temperature
1 mark: Roast beef: Yorkshire pudding and horseradish sauce
1 mark: Roast pork: apple sauce (and sage and onion stuffing)
1 mark: Roast chicken: bread sauce, game chips, stuffing
questions.explanation: Roasting is dry-heat oven or spit cooking with fat and basting. Use tender cuts, seal in a hot oven, baste and rest the meat. Beef: Yorkshire pudding and horseradish; pork: apple sauce; chicken: bread sauce.

questions.topic: Types of food service and table laying/setting
questions.stem: Describe each of the following types of food service: (a) silver service; (b) buffet service; (c) banquet service; (d) vending. [8 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Silver service: waiter serves food from a flat or dish onto the guest's plate at the table using a service spoon and fork
2 marks: Buffet: food displayed on tables; guests serve themselves or are served at the buffet
2 marks: Banquet: formal function in which a large number of guests are served the same menu at the same time
2 marks: Vending: food and drinks dispensed by automatic machines, usually by inserting money or a card
questions.explanation: Silver service uses spoon and fork to serve from a dish at the table; buffet is self-service from a display; banquet serves many guests one menu simultaneously; vending uses automatic machines.

questions.stem:
A caterer prepares 12 portions of jollof rice with chicken. The ingredients cost ₦9,000.
(a) Calculate the food cost per portion. [2 marks]
(b) If each portion sells for ₦1,500, calculate the gross profit on the 12 portions. [3 marks]
(c) State three methods of portion control. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Cost per portion = ₦9,000 / 12 = ₦750
1 mark: Total sales = 12 x ₦1,500 = ₦18,000
2 marks: Gross profit = ₦18,000 - ₦9,000 = ₦9,000
3 marks: Any three (1 each): use standard recipes; standard serving utensils (ladles, scoops); pre-portioned items; standard plates/dishes; weighing portions; staff training
questions.explanation: Cost per portion ₦750; sales ₦18,000; gross profit ₦9,000 (50% of sales). Portion control uses standard recipes, ladles and scoops, pre-portioned items and standard dishes.

questions.stem:
(a) Distinguish between a table d'hote menu and an a la carte menu. [4 marks]
(b) State four factors to consider when planning a menu for a school boarding house. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Table d'hote: fixed price for a set meal with limited choice, served at a set time
2 marks: A la carte: wide choice, each dish priced separately and cooked to order, so longer waiting time
4 marks: Any four (1 each): nutritional needs of the students; age and activity level; budget/cost; religious and cultural considerations; availability and season of foods; equipment and staff; variety and balance
questions.explanation: Table d'hote is a fixed-price set menu with limited choice; a la carte prices each dish separately and cooks to order. Boarding-house menus should consider nutrition, age, budget, religion, availability and variety.
